wikiGoal: A code wiki for this repository.

pages.title: Architecture overview
pages.purpose: High-level map of the repository's systems and how they relate: the website-automation-builder generator, the generated site-template runtime it emits, the cardmarket-automation generated skill as a worked instance, and the repo-level setup/CI layer. Clarify what is a generator (builder) vs. a product of generation (cardmarket, demo) vs. a meta skill (setup).
instructions: Use a mermaid diagram to show the generation relationship (builder -> site-template instance -> cardmarket/demo) and the runtime execution layer. Clearly distinguish generator code, generated artifacts, and meta skills so an agent edits the right place.

pages.title: Page Object Model and state-driven navigation
pages.purpose: The state model of the generated runtime: each POM represents a browser page/state, page-to-page and in-page transitions are expressed as POM methods, and documentation stages are intended to match code states. Covers the SitePage base, page subclasses, filter objects, URL construction, and parsing, and how selectors and state stages align between references and code.
instructions: Use a mermaid state diagram for page/state transitions (in-page actions vs navigation to another POM). Reflect the TODO intent that code states and documentation states should match, and note that selector/stage alignment is an invariant to preserve.

pages.title: Site runtime and execution contract
pages.purpose: The core reusable engine generated for each site: engine, cli-browser, browser-entry, manifest, observation, build-state, fingerprint, guards, errors, and input. Explains how the runtime attaches to an already-open browser via the pinned Playwright CLI, executes precompiled TypeScript/POM actions, manages build-state and fingerprints, handles errors, and enforces write/determinism safety. This is the single most important page for making safe changes.
instructions: Use a mermaid sequence diagram for the runtime request flow (input -> manifest/observation -> action -> build-state -> output). Document the pinned Playwright CLI version 0.1.19, attach-only (never launch/replace/close the browser) invariant, deterministic waiting, and the write-safety rules. Preserve the full failure/error-handling behavior. State that source code and tests are authoritative.

pages.title: Skill model and portability contract
pages.purpose: Explain the governing model for every skill in the repo: progressive disclosure (name+description, then full SKILL.md), the portability constraint that agents only need to read SKILL.md and run a local node site-runtime process, and the rule that generated skills require no harness-specific tools or plugins. Documents the SKILL.md frontmatter contract and reference-directory layout.
instructions: Emphasize the portability and no-extra-tools invariants and how they constrain what may be added to a skill. Note that reference docs are the authoritative detail layer.

pages.title: Playwright CLI integration
pages.purpose: The external integration that makes the generated skills work: the pinned Playwright CLI (0.1.19) and how the runtime attaches to an already-open browser via playwright-cli, its session/storage-state management, and how observations and element attributes are obtained from it. Captures the version-pinning invariant and the attach-only (never launch/replace/close) constraint.
instructions: State the Playwright CLI version pin (0.1.19) as an invariant and flag any version-sensitive behavior. Emphasize attach-only semantics and that the CLI is a user-scoped global dependency. Note that the pinned references live under the cardmarket node_modules copy.

pages.title: Setup, prerequisites, and CI
pages.purpose: Repository operations: the /setup skill's audit-then-install contract (read-only check first, install in dependency order, re-audit, report), the required and conditional prerequisites (Node >=22.16.0, Task, pinned Playwright CLI 0.1.19, OpenWiki, cardmarket deps, Chrome extension conditional), the Taskfile tasks (setup:check, test, install:opencode, openwiki:update), and the GitHub Actions CI path. Covers OpenWiki update workflow and the do-not-hand-edit rule for generated pages.
instructions: Preserve the setup contract: audit before installing, install only missing/incompatible items, re-audit, and never run openwiki --init or attach/launch a browser automatically. Treat network/global installs as approval-bearing. Note the Playwright CLI pin (0.1.19) and that an unexpected version is incompatible.

pages.title: Cardmarket automation skill
pages.purpose: The maintained generated skill for Cardmarket (MTG): its read-only action surface (cards.search result tiles, cards.price detail + seller offers, cards.artworks print variants), the planned user-offers state and navigation (Selling -> My offers -> Singles, card-name filter, pagination, offer detail comparison), and its references (actions, flows, selectors, verification) and example inputs.
instructions: Document the action surface and flows as user-facing capabilities and the user-offers state as planned/TODO (see TODOs.md). Distinguish verified read-only actions from planned mutating states, and note the attach-only Playwright CLI behavior and the pinned version.

pages.title: Testing and verification
pages.purpose: The browser-free verification strategy across the repo: the builder regression suite (test-scaffold, test-demo, the demo's fixture server, fake-playwright-cli/fake-process-list, and runtime.integration.test.ts), the cardmarket unit tests (actions, cli, engine, fingerprint, guards, input, parse, seller-filters), and how live-browser evidence is kept separate from the automated, browser-free checks run by `task test` and CI.
instructions: Prefer the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior, and preserve complete failure output. Clearly separate the browser-free regression suite from live-browser evidence and map each test file to the behavior it guards.

pages.title: Builder generation pipeline
pages.purpose: End-to-end workflow for the website-automation-builder: from intake and site discovery, through POM/selector authoring, runtime and build-state generation, preflight, scaffold, demo instantiation, and verification — to producing a portable generated skill. Explains what scripts/scaffold.mjs and preflight.mjs do and how the demo and site-template relate to the generated output.
instructions: Use a mermaid flow diagram for the generation pipeline (intake -> discovery -> author POM/actions -> scaffold -> demo -> verify). Call out the generated-skill-contract as the target spec the pipeline must satisfy, and keep the browser-free regression path distinct from live-browser evidence.

pages.title: Runtime execution and action dispatch
pages.purpose: The runtime behavior of a generated skill in use: how the CLI parses input, selects an action, drives the POM/state transitions through the engine, observes results, and emits output. Uses the cardmarket skill as the concrete example, showing its cli, action index, and lib glue (auth, state, url, parse).
instructions: Use a mermaid sequence diagram for a single action invocation from CLI to output. Show how actions map to POM transitions and how observation/fingerprint gate execution. Reference the runtime contract for authoritative invariants.

pages.title: Quickstart: repository overview and task routing
pages.purpose: Entry point that orients a coding agent to this skills collection: what the repo is (a reusable agent-skill library), its three owned systems (the website-automation-builder generator, the generated cardmarket-automation skill, and the setup/CI scaffolding), how to get running, and a routing map into the architecture, concepts, workflows, testing, and operations pages.
instructions: This is the routing hub: briefly introduce each owned system and the key cross-system relationship (builder generates cardmarket), then route readers to the other pages. Include how to get the repo running (task setup:check / task test) at a high level.
